method: Complete pinned AVX2 C source read with Git/SHA256 verification. Source-only; ARM NEON parity is not reused as AVX2 runtime evidence.
findings: Degree8 hash_many batches use unaligned32-byte loads/stores and transpose eight message lanes before seven rounds. Each input must contain blocks*64 readable bytes; final partial-block handling belongs to upper layers.

Counters add lane offsets0..7 only when increment requested; unsigned32 carry is implemented by sign-bit XOR before signed compare, then subtracting all-ones carry mask from high word. Boundary correctness still requires actual AVX2 execution.

Outer counter increments by8 per batch and output advances8*32. Remaining0..7 inputs delegate to SSE4.1 unless disabled, then portable implementation. Source references do not prove that linked fallback exists or was selected correctly.

storeu parameter annotation says dest[16] but intrinsic writes32 bytes; actual call sites stride sizeof(__m256i)=32 and allocate output contract accordingly. Annotation mismatch alone is not an overflow proof.
Prefetch targets block_offset+256 for all eight input lanes, including near end. No architectural read-fault or performance claim from prefetch syntax alone.
Flags_start applies first full block, flags_end last, base flags apply all blocks. Zero-block calls preserve key state and require caller contract assessment; no empty-file digest claim.
Runtime CPU/OS feature gating lives in previously reviewed dispatcher, not this function. Compiling this file cannot establish safe instruction dispatch on arbitrary hardware.
x86 assembly variants are separate unread blobs; reading intrinsics C does not count their review or their ABI/counter correctness.
limits: No AVX2 compilation/execution, sanitizer coverage or speed measurement on this ARM host.
